questionsToConsider: Which company traits actually change how you sell or what you build: size, sector, region or business model?
Do you need a revenue band at all, or does headcount tell you enough?
Which currency and revenue bands fit the companies you usually talk to?
Do you want to use this for research only, or also to pass interested respondents to sales?
guide.howToUseResponses: Treat each response as a company profile and build segments from the combinations that matter, such as mid-sized B2B firms in professional services. Compare those segments against your other research or deal history rather than assuming every company of one size behaves the same. Send the respondents who asked for a follow-up to sales with their buying role, so the first call starts at the right level.
customizeSteps: Trim the industry list to the sectors you sell into, keeping an Other option, and set the revenue bands and currency to match your market.
Remove the follow-up question if this is pure research, so nobody feels the survey was a sales form in disguise.
Embed it on a resource or research page, or send it to an existing list, then export responses to CSV to segment them.

faqs.a: Facts that describe an organisation, such as industry, size, revenue, location and business model. They do for companies what demographics do for people.

faqs.q: What firmographic questions should I ask?
faqs.a: Industry, number of employees, revenue band, headquarters location, number of sites and who the company sells to. Add the respondent's team and buying role if the results feed sales.

faqs.q: Should I ask for exact revenue?
faqs.a: No. Bands are easier to answer and just as useful for segmenting. Make the question optional, since some people cannot share it.

faqs.q: How do I use firmographic data in marketing?
faqs.a: Group respondents into segments by the traits that change their needs, then tailor messages, offers and sales focus to each group instead of treating every business the same.
